t: The Company and the Nawab each had aims: the Company wanted recognition of its privileges and reparation for Calcutta, and Siraj-ud-Daulah wanted to stop the unauthorised fortifications and the loss of his revenue.
The Company's side won with a small force because of a conspiracy: Mir Jafar, Rai Durlabh and Yar Lutuf Khan brought their troops to the field but made no move, and the Nawab fled.
To deal with the merchant Omichund, Clive had two treaties drawn up, a real one on white paper and a false one on red, and Admiral Watson's signature on the false one was counterfeited.
dyk: Clive's two treaties, a real one on white paper and a false one on red to deceive Omichund, were signed by the Company's committee, but Admiral Watson signed only the real one, and his signature on the other had to be counterfeited.
ev: Alivardi Khan dies and is succeeded by his grandson Siraj-ud-Daulah, aged twenty-three
Siraj-ud-Daulah takes Calcutta, and many of the prisoners die in the Black Hole
Clive and Admiral Watson recapture Calcutta on 2 January
Clive takes the French town of Chandannagar
Mir Jafar signs the treaties with the Company on 4 June
The battle is fought on 23 June; Mir Jafar is saluted as Nawab the next day
Siraj-ud-Daulah is betrayed at Rajmahal on 2 July and murdered that night by Mir Jafar's son Miran's order
The Company defeats a Dutch force at Chinsura and replaces Mir Jafar with Mir Qasim

f.date: 23 June 1757; the fighting is said to have ended in approximately 11 hours
f.place: Palashi (Anglicised Plassey) on the banks of the Hooghly River, about 150 kilometres (93 mi) north of Calcutta and south of Murshidabad, in West Bengal, India
f.sides: The British East India Company under Colonel Robert Clive, with about 3,000 soldiers (some 750 European infantry, 2,100 sepoys and artillery), and a small French contingent on the other side; the Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah, with about 50,000 soldiers including the defectors (30,000 infantry and 20,000 cavalry by the fuller count), 10 war elephants, and artillery put at anything from 40 to 300 pieces.
f.outcome: The Nawab's army dispersed and Siraj-ud-Daulah fled; the Company occupied his camp. Clive estimated the Nawab's losses at 500 men, and British losses were estimated at 22 killed and 50 wounded, with 13 sepoys killed and 30 wounded.
